findings.title: Signal subsystem grows oversized BaseAgentAdapter
findings.problem: code-quality.md Code Structure Guidelines (files under 500 lines, one main export, single responsibility) are further breached by new code: the change adds a self-contained signal-forwarding and output-stream-guard subsystem (SIGNAL_FALLBACK_MS, SignalHandlers, onOutputStreamError, ignoreClosedOutputStreams, signalChildTree, installWin32/PosixSignalHandlers, lines 40-102 and 1020-1126) to a file now 1583 lines, plus a second, test-only export resetOutputStreamGuardForTests that mutates global process state from a production module.
findings.impact: The documented structure standard is breached by code this change introduces, not pre-existing code; the signal subsystem is a separable responsibility, and its test-only reset is callable from production code.
findings.recommendation: Move SIGNAL_FALLBACK_MS, the SignalHandlers interface, the output-stream guard (onOutputStreamError, ignoreClosedOutputStreams, resetOutputStreamGuardForTests), signalChildTree and the win32/POSIX handler installers into a sibling module (e.g. src/agents/core/signal-handlers.ts) and import them into BaseAgentAdapter, so the adapter keeps a single main export.

findings.title: Windows SIGHUP kill throws and crashes wrapper
findings.problem: installWin32SignalHandlers registers process.once('SIGHUP') (emitted by Node on console close) and its handler calls child.kill('SIGHUP'). On win32 libuv's process kill supports only SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGKILL/SIGQUIT (and 0) and returns UV_ENOSYS for any other signal, and Node's ChildProcess.kill throws an ErrnoException on ENOSYS/EINVAL rather than emitting 'error'. The throw escapes a process signal listener with no try/catch.
findings.impact: On Windows console close the wrapper dies with an uncaught exception before the child is killed and before the exit path runs grace, session end and proxy stop, so the session is not finalized - the exact crash-on-terminal-close scenario this change exists to fix. The win32 SIGHUP test mocks child.kill, so CI cannot catch it. Basis: Node/libuv win32 kill semantics, not executed on Windows in this review.
findings.recommendation: In installWin32SignalHandlers never pass SIGHUP to child.kill: map it to a signal Windows supports (e.g. `child.kill(signal === 'SIGHUP' ? 'SIGTERM' : signal)`), and wrap the call in try/catch logging at debug so no throw escapes a process signal listener. Make the win32 test assert the signal actually passed to child.kill is one of SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGKILL/SIGQUIT.

findings.title: SIGINT unbounded wait and Windows terminate vs ticket
findings.problem: The ticket's Expected Result requires the wrapper to forward SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to the agent and wait, bounded, for its exit and SessionEnd. forwardSignal returns before arming the fallback when signal === 'SIGINT', so an agent that ignores SIGINT is waited for indefinitely; on win32 installWin32SignalHandlers terminates the child outright with child.kill instead of forwarding, so the agent's own SessionEnd cannot run there. The PR's Scope (and the run's task statement) reinterpret the AC; the ticket text was not amended.
findings.impact: Shipping with a required story criterion only partially met: a wrapper whose agent ignores SIGINT never finishes, and Windows sessions rely solely on the wrapper's own finalization. Whether that is acceptable is a product decision the code cannot settle.
findings.recommendation: Get product/ticket-owner sign-off on the PR's Scope reinterpretation (SIGINT forwarded with no bounded wait; Windows terminates the agent rather than forwarding for its own SessionEnd) and record it on the ticket; if sign-off is refused, arm the 10 s fallback for SIGINT too and document the Windows limit against the AC.

findings.title: Self-exit CODEMIE_EXIT_SIGNAL path untested
findings.problem: Regression gap: the rewritten `const exitSignal = fallbackSignal() ?? signal;` (BaseAgentAdapter.ts:971) is asserted only on fallback-fired paths (tests at :206, :226, :273). The test at :186, where the agent exits on its own after a forwarded SIGTERM (`child.emit('exit', null, 'SIGTERM')`), checks events, rejection and timer count but never exitSignals, so losing the `?? signal` branch would pass CI.
findings.impact: The consumer is Pi's session-end reason built from env.CODEMIE_EXIT_SIGNAL (src/agents/plugins/pi/pi.plugin.ts:463): a regression would silently stop reporting signal(SIGTERM) for agents that exit cleanly on a forwarded signal.
findings.recommendation: In the 'forwards SIGTERM before any cleanup, then ends the session and stops the proxy once' test, after the run rejects add `expect(exitSignals).toEqual(['SIGTERM'])`, so the `fallbackSignal() ?? signal` branch for an agent that exits on its own is pinned.
